pairs: Ecce omnia hæc vidit oculus meus,
Behold, my eye has seen all these things,
et audivit auris mea, et intellexi singula.
and my ear has heard, and I have understood each one.
I am not inferior to you.
Yet I speak this way to the Almighty,
and I desire to argue with God,
having first shown that you fabricate lies
And I wish that you would remain silent,
so that you would be counted among the wise.
and pay attention to the judgment of my lips.
so that you would speak deceitfully for him?
and do you struggle to give judgment in favor of God?
aut placebit ei quem celare nihil potest?
Or, will it please him, from whom nothing can be concealed?
Ipse vos arguet, quoniam in abscondito faciem ejus accipitis.
He will accuse you because in secret you have preempted his presence.
As soon as he moves himself,
et terror ejus irruet super vos.
and his dread will fall over you.
Your remembrance will be compared to ashes,
et redigentur in lutum cervices vestræ.
and your necks will be reduced to clay.
Be silent for a little while,
ut loquar quodcumque mihi mens suggesserit.
so that I may speak whatever my mind suggests to me.
Quare lacero carnes meas dentibus meis,
Why do I wound my flesh with my teeth,
et animam meam porto in manibus meis?
and carry my soul in my hands?
And now, if he would kill me,
verumtamen vias meas in conspectu ejus arguam.
in this, truly, I will correct my ways in his sight.
And he will be my savior,
non enim veniet in conspectu ejus omnis hypocrita.
for no hypocrite at all will approach in his sight.
and perceive an enigma with your ears.
I know that I will be found to be just.
Who is it that will go to judgment with me?
Why should I be consumed in silence?
Do not do such things to me twice,
et tunc a facie tua non abscondar:
and then I will not hide from your face.
manum tuam longe fac a me,
Take your hand far away from me,
et formido tua non me terreat.
and do not let your dread terrify me.
How many iniquities and sins do I have?
scelera mea et delicta ostende mihi.
Reveal my crimes and offenses to me.
Why do you conceal your face
and consider me to be your enemy?
which is carried away by the wind,
For you write bitter things against me,
et consumere me vis peccatis adolescentiæ meæ.
and you want to consume me for the sins of my youth.
You have put my feet on a tether,
and you have observed all my paths,
and you have considered the steps of my feet.
I will be left to decay like something rotten
et quasi vestimentum quod comeditur a tinea.
and like a garment that is being eaten by moths.
